findings.reason: the plan needs `reckon/crew/gc.py` (or a marker the reap respects) in its write paths and in its done-when, otherwise it ships a route that a routine gc pass silently defeats.
findings.text: §5 asserts "Today nothing retires that pointer" and concludes the kept pointer survives "until the head reaches the branch", but `crew gc`'s live-pointer reap unlinks any pointer whose run id is in the ledger and whose process is not alive (`reckon/crew/gc.py:722-739`: `if record_run_id not in ledgered or record_process_alive(record) is not False: continue` … `pointer_path(record_run_id).unlink()`); a run promoted with the separate-merge flag has a ledger row and a dead worker, so an ordinary gc pass removes the pointer before the merge and `crew merge --run` loses the run exactly as in nova-8a — the failure §5 exists to prevent. The done-when's second case cannot detect this because it never runs gc between promotion and merge

findings.reason: without a §5 followup the plan's declared chain cannot start, and §6 is undeliverable through it.
findings.text: §5 is declared `implementable` and §6 waits on it (`plan-section-depends-on` s6→s5, plan.html:29), but no followup carries `/reckon-build a-landing-is-on-main-when-it-says-so §5`; the only open followup (f-alomwiss-006) dispatches §6, so a coordinator following the plan's own chain queues a node whose upstream nothing drives, and the admit service holds §6 `awaiting-upstream` indefinitely

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `crew_merge` is at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:251`, `merge.land_merge` at `:329` and `merge.py` contains no pointer removal, `pending_landing.finish_pending_landings` is at `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:187` with the live-run skip at `:233`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when names two negative controls (base revision promotes and removes the pointer; skipping the retirement leaves the pointer on disk), both of which can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 names no scratchpad or node-local path; its measure is a repository test file plus the run-directory log convention the plan states in §2 and §6.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces no plan label, stage name or ticket number into a symbol, file or comment; the separate-merge flag is described by what it does.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the mechanism's premise "Today nothing retires that pointer" is false: `crew gc` reaps every live pointer whose run has a ledger row and whose process is not alive (`reckon/crew/gc.py:722-739`), which is exactly the state a separate-merge promotion leaves behind.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable: a plain complete neither promotes an unmerged head nor leaves the kept run unresolvable, with the retirement as the same behaviour's second half.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 is declared implementable (plan.html:23) and §6 declares `plan-section-depends-on` s6→s5 (plan.html:29), but no followup names §5; the only open followup is f-alomwiss-006, whose prompt dispatches §6 (plan.html:80-84).
